body.statement: The finite-sample one-batch frontier obeys the identity \[\Psi^{=}_{n,1}=\min_{k\in\{\lceil n/4\rceil,\ldots,\lfloor3n/4\rfloor\}}\ \sup_{\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in[\ell,u]}\left\{\frac{\sigma_1^2}{k/n}+\frac{\sigma_0^2}{1-k/n}-V^*(\sigma)\right\}.\] Here each \(k\) corresponds to the constant singleton-domain policy \(q_1(\varnothing)=k\). A nearest-to-balanced count is minimax. With \(p_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor/n\le1/2\), a complete case split over the clipped-oracle regions \(\sigma_1/\sigma_0<1/3\), \(\sigma_1/\sigma_0\in[1/3,3]\), and \(\sigma_1/\sigma_0>3\) gives \[\Psi^{=}_{n,1}=\frac{u^2}{p_n}+\frac{\ell^2}{1-p_n}-V^*(\sigma)\big|_{\sigma_1=u,\,\sigma_0=\ell}.\] For odd \(n\), this is exactly \[\frac{2nu^2}{n-1}+\frac{2n\ell^2}{n+1}-V^*(\sigma)\big|_{\sigma_1=u,\,\sigma_0=\ell};\] the ceiling count has the symmetric opposite worst orientation and the same minimax value. For even \(n\), the two variance orientations tie at \(p_n=1/2\), and explicit evaluation of the clipped oracle yields \[\Psi^{=}_{n,1}=\begin{cases}(u-\ell)^2,&u\le3\ell,\\ 2u^2/3-2\ell^2,&u\ge3\ell,\end{cases}\] continuously at \(u=3\ell\). In particular, the second value also arises at \(\sigma_1=u,\sigma_0=\ell\) and is not zero there. For two batches, \(\Psi^{=}_{n,2}\asymp n^{-1/2}\) uniformly over the fixed parameter box; an attaining-order construction uses a balanced pilot of order \(n^{1/2}\), a clipped exact-count plug-in second wave, and an admissible deterministic weight choice.
body.justification: Closed one- and two-wave anchors prevent the general frontier from hiding an incorrect endpoint or pilot exponent.
body.gap: Cai and Rafi analyze fixed pilots, Yamin gives a boundary-driven global pilot rate, and Zhao gives an upper exponent; none jointly treats the nondegenerate Gaussian interior, exact counts, deterministic weights, and a matching two-wave lower bound.
body.consumer: Two-wave experiments can use the square-root pilot as a principled default while quantifying when one-wave balance is preferable.
